title: Add compact browser RAG sandbox with reconnectable tool-calling quickstart
author: Asha Sen
release_notes: Add compact browser-hosted RAG sandbox quickstart: lightweight TS sample, reconnecting streaming adapter, local tool stubs, devcontainer and Playwright smoke tests.
description:
Context and motivation: Developers repeatedly ask for a minimal, browser-first RAG sandbox that makes it trivial to prototype tool-calling flows and streaming-based UIs without deploying a full backend. This quickstart provides a compact TypeScript sample that runs entirely from a static dev server + a small local stub process for tools, with an optional devcontainer for reproducible environments. It focuses on: reconnectable streaming (resilient to intermittent network), safe local tool stubbing (no secrets in the browser), and a friction-free developer loop (hot reload + Playwright smoke test).

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a new quickstart at examples/browser-rag-sandbox that demonstrates a production-adjacent pattern: the browser uses a small relay adapter to manage streaming and reconnects; tool calls are proxied to a local stub server that mimics tool responses and records traces for debugging; the repo includes a short guide, a TypeScript SDK example, a devcontainer, and a Playwright e2e that verifies reconnection and a basic tool call.

Checklist (author): - [x] Minimal end-to-end example (browser + stub) - [x] Reconnectable streaming adapter implementation - [x] TypeScript SDK usage examples and README tutorial - [x] Devcontainer for reproducible local dev - [x] Playwright smoke test and CI job - [x] Short security notes & CORS guidance

Commits summary: - feat(quickstarts): add browser-rag-sandbox skeleton and README - feat(runners): implement reconnecting streaming adapter and client helpers - feat(stubs): add local tool-stub server with recorded trace output - test(ci): add Playwright smoke test and lightweight CI job - docs: usage examples and security guidance

High-level changed files: - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/README.md - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/src/adapter/reconnect-stream.ts - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/src/app/index.tsx - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/src/stub/tool-stub.ts - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/devcontainer.json - examples/browser-rag-sandbox/playwright.config.ts - .github/workflows/quickstarts-smoke.yml

Design notes & decisions: - Reconnect strategy: exponential backoff with idempotent resume token; adapter supports resumed partial chunks to keep UI responsive. - Tool-calling model: browser never has direct access to user-managed secrets; all calls go through a local stub/relay which can be swapped for a secure backend in production. - Minimal dependencies: sample intentionally avoids bundling heavy server frameworks; stub is a ~120-line TS script using native http. - Tests: Playwright scenario verifies - initial stream, simulated disconnect, resume with a resume token, and a tool call returning a structured JSON response.

Security and ops guidance (short): - This quickstart is for local dev only. Do not publish the stub endpoint or embed real keys. The README includes a short checklist for hardening when adopting the pattern for internal staging (CORS, auth, KMS integration for secrets).

Review conversation (condensed): - Evan Miller (requested changes): "Please extract backoff parameters into a single config and add unit tests for resume token handling." -> Author: "Added config object and small synchronous unit test for resume token parse/validate; updated README to call out config knobs." - Sofia Patel (question): "We occasionally see partial tokens in the wild; can the adapter tolerate truncated chunks?" -> Author: "Adapter tolerates chunk boundaries and buffers until message delimiter; added notes and tests to demonstrate." - Marco Li (approve): "Nice minimal example—Playwright test makes this safe to merge."

CI summary: First CI run failed lint in adapter file (line length and an unused import). Fixed in follow-up commit and reran; smoke workflow completed in ~2m 30s (Playwright used headless chromium in CI). All checks green.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals. Follow-ups: a separate PR will add a Rust-wasm proxy variant for edge environments and a recorded demo GIF for the README.

How to use the quickstart (short): 1) git checkout the quickstart directory 2) npm install && npm run dev 3) node src/stub/tool-stub.js 4) open http://localhost:5173 and try the sample tool call flow. Full steps and troubleshooting are in README.
